text:
jen: Hey team — PR https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/57813 is ready for review. It’s a small change to the KV prefetch logic that should reduce cold-start latencies for short sequences. Requesting runtime + infra eyes and security signoff for the auth headers tweak. Can folks volunteer?

alex: I can take runtime. Quick ask — does this change the eviction behavior or only prefetch TTL?

jen: Only TTL + a tiny reordering guard. No eviction policy changes. Tests included.

chris: I’ll take infra but need the perf numbers. Can you paste the microbench output?

jen: Pasted below: `bench/cold_start_1000runs: median 18ms -> 12ms (prefetch on)` and `mem: +0.8%`. Full results in the PR CI artifact.

maya: cc @nina (security) — there’s a header ordering touch in handler_auth.go. Nina, is a short threat-model note + ACK enough or do you want a follow-up ticket?

nina: I’ll review. If it only changes ordering and we don’t change allowed headers, an ACK + a quick note in the PR should suffice. Confirm there’s no new surface for header duplication.

jen: Confirmed — we append a normalized header set and dedupe. No new header names.

ci-bot: CI: all checks passed ✅ (unit, integration, lint). Perf artifacts uploaded to https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/57813.

alex: skimmed the runtime diff — one minor comment about a nil-check I left inline. Otherwise LGTM from runtime side pending that tiny fix.

chris: infra ok with the microbench numbers. Can we schedule the canary for tomorrow at 09:00 PT? I’ll own the rollback step.

jen: Tomorrow 09:00 PT works for me. @maya do you want to gate platform rollout or let it go with infra canary?

maya: Let infra canary run first. Platform will monitor token-level latency and error rates. I’ll be standing by.

nina: security ACK from me, added comment about audit log entry but not blocking.

jen: Thanks all — I’ll fix the nil-check and merge once alex re-approves. Rolling canary window set for 2025-04-02 09:00 PT.

alex: fixed the nil-check, re-requesting review.

jen: got the approve from runtime — merging in 5m and tagging canary owners. :shipit:
